Evidence (2026-10-31 PDT, host temp dir /var/folders/.../T, file contents never read or printed):

Host census: 621 `rebar-opcert-*` dirs (575 when filed). By modification date: 144 on 10-28, 135 on 10-29, 144 on 10-30, 198 on 10-31. 276 of 621 also hold `opcert-key.pub`. 0 `rebar-opcert-ws-*` dirs. A full `lsof` shows 0 open files under any `rebar-opcert-*` dir; no `rebar-mcp` process runs on this host.

Per-module before count, each module run alone at 1c51c9dcd06 with TMPDIR set to an empty sandbox (`pytest -n0`), all passing:
- test_opcert_service_integrity_heldout: 1 left (1 with .pub)
- test_opcert_service: 8 left (3 with .pub)
- test_rp04_s6_opcert_startup: 0
- test_mcp_opcert_signing_goose: 0
- test_mcp_drain_signing_iguanodon: 0
- test_opcert_privkey_env_pop_932d: 0
- test_opcert_service_app: 0

The 2 leaking modules pass `signer=_signer(tmp_path)` straight into `run_job` and never call `cleanup()`. Sandbox .pub ratio 4/9 (44%) matches the host's 276/621 (44%), consistent with these tests as the host source. 9 per suite run at ~150 per day corresponds to about 16 local runs of those modules per day across sessions.

Prior intent: no earlier tracker ticket covers this leak (`rebar search` for rebar-opcert / signer cleanup / compose_signer). mempalace (wing rebar) returned 8 drawers whose text is stored compressed and was not readable in this session, so it gave no usable prior decision. The keyprov module docstring already assigns removal to the signer's owner via `cleanup()`; the fix follows that.
